meta.title: Government support
meta.question: Do Poles support the government of the day?
meta.measure: Average support for the government of the day, from 0 (opponent) to 10 (supporter)
meta.anchor: Pooled from every question on support for and satisfaction with the government of the day, whichever it is, with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

items.wording: Does the activity of the government (Council of Ministers) serve society well? (institutions battery)
items.notes: CBOS, 1990-01 to 1997-08, 49 surveys (institutions battery: does the government's activity serve society well?). Covers the Mazowiecki, Bielecki and Olszewski governments before CBOS_GOV_STANCE starts.

items.wording: How satisfied are you with the present government? (1-10)
items.notes: CDCEE Jan 1991 (Bielecki government) and Mar 2000 (Buzek government), 1-10.

items.wording: Would you greet news of the present government's resignation with satisfaction, indifference or dissatisfaction?
items.notes: CBOS, 1992-09 to 2004-02, 27 surveys. Satisfaction at the news of resignation = 0, indifference = 5, dissatisfaction = 10.

items.wording: How would you describe your attitude to the (present / PM's) government: decided supporter, moderate supporter, moderate opponent, decided opponent, or indifferent?
items.notes: CBOS, 1992-12 to 2017-12, 291 surveys (almost monthly). The label names the PM from 2004 (Belka, Marcinkiewicz, Kaczyński, Tusk, Kopacz, Szydło); 'indifferent' (5) = 5. 2008-09 labels carry '1)' prefixes.

items.wording: How satisfied are you with the way the people now in national office are handling the country's affairs?
items.notes: WVS 1997 only (people in national office handling the country's affairs).

items.wording: Attitude to the government: supporter, opponent or indifferent (PGSW 2000; CBOS wording)
items.notes: PGSW 2000 presidential study (attit038), CBOS stance wording (Buzek government).

items.wording: How well has the (outgoing) government performed? (very well ... very badly)
items.notes: PGSW 2001, 2005, 2007, 2019, 2023. Post-election surveys: the government rated is the outgoing one (still in office at fieldwork, except possibly late interviews in 2005 and 2023).

items.wording: What kind of influence is our national government having on the way things are going in the country? (very good ... very bad)
items.notes: Pew, Polish readings 2002, 2007, 2014 (the regex also matches 2009-13 and 2015, when Poland was not asked; in 2012 it matches a second, Japan-only variable). Evaluation of the national government's influence on how things are going.

items.wording: How satisfied are you with the national government? (0-10)
Do you approve or disapprove of the government's record to date?
items.notes: European Election Studies 2004, 2009, 2014, 2019. 2004 code 3 'neither [spain]' has no position.

items.wording: How do you rate the government's activity over the last four years? (online)
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker waves 4, 9, 10 (2020-21), online. Rates the government over the last four years.

items.wording: Generally speaking, how do you rate the government's activity? (SWPS omnibus 2020)
Attitude to the Morawiecki government (CBOS democracy survey 2021)
items.notes: CBOS democracy survey, c. 2021 (q37, Morawiecki government).

items.wording: How satisfied are you with the national government? (0-10)
items.notes: ESS round 10 (2021-22): self-completion by web and paper in Poland, where every other round was face to face, so a question of its own.

items.wording: Do you approve or disapprove of the government's record to date?
How well has the government performed? (2025 presidential study)
Attitude to the Tusk government: supporter, opponent or indifferent (CBOS wording)
items.notes: PGSW 2025 presidential study; CBOS stance wording.
